messages.subject: summary scantwo/epistasis/LODS
messages.body_plain:
Hi

I need help to interpret summary of plot.scantwo. I’m interested in
epistatic interactions LOD scores to put in my write up. We did not
choose any LOD scores threshold so we just did it based on 0.05.

Normally for QTL I use LOD score of 2 for significance but if want to
say we have significant epistatic interaction which of these LOD score
I should I use? Fo all of these4 traits I can see significant
interaction between marker in effect plots but I need LOD scores to
include in my write up to make it more statistical meaningful.

Phenotypes	chr1	chr2	pos1f	pos2f	lod.full	lod.fv1	lod.int <http://lod.int>	pos1a	pos2a
lod.add	lod.av1
XX1	4	9	50	80	3.515	1.313	0.345	50	80	3.17	0.968
XX2	3	7	80	60	6.872	2.914	1.090	40	60	5.78	1.824
XX3	4	9	120	20	5.322	1.079	0.027	120	20	5.3	1.053

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] summary scantwo/epistasis/LODS
messages.body_plain:
There is a relatively complete discussion of the interpretation of scantwo results at the following:

  http://www.rqtl.org/tutorials/new_summary_scantwo.pdf

In general, I would recommend the use of a fixed threshold (like 2) for LOD scores; the appropriate threshold depends on the nature of the cross, the size of the genome, and the type of LOD score.  So while a threshold of 3.5 might be appropriate for a single-QTL genome scan in an intercross, the appropriate threshold for a LOD score assessing an epistatic interaction would be completely different.

I like to use permutation tests to define relevant thresholds (or, even better, to assign genome-scan-adjusted p-values to LOD scores).  For these scantwo analyses, that means having to do a permutation test with a two-dimensional, two-QTL genome scan.  This can be quite computationally intensive, though if Haley-Knott regression (method="hk" in scantwo) is appropriate for your data, the permutation test would be considerably faster than with other methods.

For the three pairs of loci you displayed, the interaction LOD scores are 0.3, 1.1 and 0.03.  None of these are likely to be seen to be significant, and so I am surprised to hear that the interactions are clear in the effect plots.

karl

messages.subject: lodint{} always expands the interval to the nearest flanking markers
messages.subject_clean: lodint{} always expands the interval to the nearest flanking markers
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rqtl users,
I've just realized there is a problem with the lodint() function : it
seems that despite setting argument expandtomarker=FALSE, this always
expands interval to the nearest flanking markers.

Here is the results of CIM for chromosome 2D :

           chr       pos        lod
wPt-4413    2D   0.00000 0.02470232
gpw4480     2D  13.10000 0.32319748
wPt-8330    2D  29.90000 0.17258229
AAP_2D      2D  32.60000 0.12268467
wPt-0724    2D  46.60000 0.27102829
wPt-4144    2D  47.10001 0.37326382
FdGogat_2D  2D  51.90001 0.05880036
Ppd-D1      2D  73.80001 4.54658393
gpw332      2D  80.80001 4.68653385
cfd56       2D 115.80001 0.03105817

Based on the plot, the interval should be roughly 60-95cM. In this
example, there is no second peak above LOD-1.5 as in a previous
discussion (http://groups.google.com/group/rqtl-disc/browse_thread/
thread/c7ae1226e33b5c92/e502b57f6d0f3fa2?
lnk=gst&q=lodint#e502b57f6d0f3fa2)

Here is the results of lodint(), first using expandtomarker=FALSE then
setting this argument to TRUE

lodint(out.cim, chr=chr, drop=1.5, expandtomarkers=FALSE)
           chr       pos        lod
FdGogat_2D  2D  51.90001 0.05880036
gpw332      2D  80.80001 4.68653385
cfd56       2D 115.80001 0.03105817

lodint(out.cim, chr=chr, drop=1.5, expandtomarkers=TRUE)
           chr       pos        lod
FdGogat_2D  2D  51.90001 0.05880036
gpw332      2D  80.80001 4.68653385
cfd56       2D 115.80001 0.03105817

So lodint give me an interval estimate of 50-115cM.
I'm using the 1.18-7 version of Rqtl. Karl, could you fix the
problem ?
Cheers

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] lodint{} always expands the interval to the nearest flanking markers
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] lodint{} always expands the interval to the nearest flanking markers
messages.body_plain:
lodint() can only work with the points on the grid at which the scanone or cim output was calculated.  If those calculations were done only at the markers, then the endpoints of the interval lodint() produces will always be at markers.  If you want a more precisely defined interval, you need a more precise grid.  The grid is defined by the step argument in calc.genoprob (or in sim.geno, for scanone with method="imp").  So rerun calc.genoprob with step=1 (or even smaller), rerun cim, and then try lodint() again.

Karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Warning Error message/read.cross
messages.body_plain:
In read.cross, use genotypes=c("AA","AB","BB") and na.strings="NA"

However the file name, "tryril.csv", indicates that these are RILs, in which case you should note that R/qtl can't handle heterozygous genotypes in RIL, and must treat them as missing.  And so, aside from the "na" vs "NA", what you are doing is correct, but you need to afterwards convert from backcross (which is hopefully how the data are interpreted) to "riself" or "risib", which you can do with the functions convert2riself() or convert2risib().  For example:

  hyper <- convert2riself(hyper)

The first warning message in scantwo just says that there was an individual (or line) with missing phenotype, and so that individual was omitted from the analysis.

It's hard to know what the 0's and negative LOD scores mean without seeing the data.

karl

messages.subject: LODs for significant epistasis
messages.body_plain:
Hi

I want to asky you about which of two LOD scores I should take in
consideration inorder to have significant epistatic interataction.

According to Karl
"Mfv1(j, k) is the log10 likelihood ratio comparing the full model
with QTL on chromosomes
j and k to the single-QTL model, with a single QTL on either
chromosome j or k. Thus, it
indicates evidence for a second QTL, allowing for the possibility of
epistasis."

so do I have to take LOD.full and LOD.fv above threshold for epistatic
interaction or LOD.full and LOD.int above threshold for evidance of
epistasis.

Thanks

s

> summary(out2, alpha=c(0.05,0.20) )
Control.t1 (1000 permutations)
        full  fv1  int  add  av1
5%   6.0 4.64 4.07 4.82 2.85
20%  5.3 3.94 3.36 4.10 2.25

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] LODs for significant epistasis
messages.body_plain:
I look for LOD.full and LOD.fv1 to each be above their thresholds, and then for LOD.int to also be large.  But others may disagree.  In particular, you might just look for LOD.int to be above its threshold.

karl

messages.subject: R/qtl version 1.19-20
messages.body_plain:
A new version of R/qtl (1.19-20) has been released at its web site
(http://www.rqtl.org).  It should be on CRAN within a couple of days.

See http://www.rqtl.org/STATUS.txt for a list of changes.  The major
changes are below.

Karl Broman
kbr...@biostat.wisc.edu

------

Version 1.19, 11/29/2010:

Major changes:

  Added a tutorial on genetic map construction; find it within the
  package at docs/geneticmaps.pdf, or (more simply, probably), find it
  on the web at http://www.rqtl.org/tutorials/geneticmaps.pdf

  Added two additional formats to summary.scanone(), "tabByCol" and
  "tabByChr".  These produce tables of LOD peaks organized by LOD
  score column or by chromosome.  The tables include approximate
  confidence intervals for QTL location (as calculated by the lodint()
  or bayesint() function; which one is indicated by the new argument
  ci.function).  Here's an example:

    bp:
               chr  pos ci.low ci.high  lod  pval
    c1.loc44.5   1 47.8   35.5    85.0 3.56 0.007
    D4Mit164     4 29.5   18.8    30.6 8.09 0.000

    sqrt:
               chr  pos ci.low ci.high  lod  pval
    c1.loc44.5   1 47.8   35.5    84.8 3.63 0.007
    D4Mit164     4 29.5   17.2    30.6 8.08 0.000
